title: Ordered root subgroup coordinates on a Borel unipotent radical
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq G$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with unipotent radical $U=R_u(B)$ and positive roots $\Phi^+$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For each root $\alpha$, let $U_\alpha\subseteq G$ be the root subgroup of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. If $\Phi^+=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$ is any enumeration without repetitions, each inclusion $U_{\alpha_i}\hookrightarrow G$ factors through $U$, and multiplication is an isomorphism of $F$-schemes
$$U_{\alpha_1}\times_F\cdots\times_F U_{\alpha_r}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }U,\qquad (u_1,\ldots,u_r)\longmapsto u_1\cdots u_r.$$
It is $T$-equivariant for componentwise conjugation on the source and conjugation on $U$. For $r=0$ the source is $\operatorname{Spec}F$ and the assertion says $U=1$.

source.place: Theorem 21.68(a), printed p.445; the root subgroup parametrizations are 21.19, printed p.431. Empty-root case is included.

proof.text: Choose a regular cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ with $B=P(\lambda)$ by [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description]. The same node gives $\operatorname{Lie}(B)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle>0}\mathfrak g_\alpha$. By the convention in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], the roots occurring in this Lie algebra are exactly $\Phi^+$. Thus $n_i=\langle\alpha_i,\lambda\rangle$ is a strictly positive integer for every $i$, and the displayed sum is over our enumeration. These are integer character weights in all characteristics.

source.place: 21.68(a), proof, choice of dominant cocharacter; 21.32 and 21.35, pp.434--435.

proof.text: Let $U_\lambda$ be the subgroup of [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure]. It is a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup of $P(\lambda)=B$, so it is contained in $U=R_u(B)$ by the defining maximality of $U$ in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Choose the isomorphisms $u_{\alpha_i}:\mathbf G_a\to U_{\alpha_i}$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Over every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, their conjugation formula reads $\lambda(t)u_{\alpha_i}(a)\lambda(t)^{-1}=u_{\alpha_i}(t^{n_i}a)$. The right side extends to $t\in\mathbf A^1_A$ and is $1$ at zero. This is precisely the defining condition for $U_\lambda(A)$. Hence the inclusions of all positive root subgroups factor through $U_\lambda\subseteq U$ as subgroup schemes, including on nonreduced test algebras.

source.place: 21.68(a), multiplication lands in B_u; Definitions 13.21 and Theorem 13.33, pp.261,265--266; root formula 21.19, p.431.

proof.text: Differentiate the $T$-equivariant scheme isomorphism $U\times_F T\to B$ and projection $p:B\to T$ in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Tangent vectors to a product are pairs of dual-number points, so this gives $\operatorname{Lie}(B)=\operatorname{Lie}(U)\oplus\operatorname{Lie}(T)$ and $\ker(d p)=\operatorname{Lie}(U)$. The action of $\lambda$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$ is trivial. On $\mathfrak g_{\alpha_i}$ it is $t^{n_i}$ by step 1. Equivariance forces $(t^{n_i}-1)d p(v)=0$ over $F[t,t^{-1}]$, so $d p(v)=0$ by comparing coefficients. Since $d p$ is the identity on $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$, the decomposition from step 1 now gives $\operatorname{Lie}(U)=\bigoplus_i\mathfrak g_{\alpha_i}$.

source.place: 21.68(a), tangent-space assertion, p.445; B=U semidirect T in Theorem 16.33(d), p.336; explicit differentiation.

proof.text: Put $X=\prod_i U_{\alpha_i}$ with identity tuple $e_X$. The parametrizations in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] identify it with $\operatorname{Spec}F[z_1,\ldots,z_r]$. Thus it is affine, connected and of finite type, and smooth: the polynomial algebra is finitely presented and a map from it lifts across a square-zero quotient by lifting its variables. The point $e_X$ is fixed by componentwise conjugation, and its tangent space is $\bigoplus_i\mathfrak g_{\alpha_i}$ with $\lambda$-weights $n_i>0$. Step 2 defines the multiplication morphism $m:X\to U$. Over every test algebra, $(t u_1t^{-1})\cdots(t u_rt^{-1})=t(u_1\cdots u_r)t^{-1}$, so $m$ is $T$-equivariant and sends $e_X$ to $1$. Its differential sends $(v_i)$ to $\sum_i v_i$: on dual numbers all cross terms contain $\epsilon^2=0$. By step 3 and the specified tangent spaces of the root subgroup inclusions, this is an isomorphism.

source.place: 21.68(a), first two sentences of proof, p.445; parametrizations 21.19, p.431; explicit polynomial and dual-number calculations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-positive-weight-equivariant-inverse] to $m:X\to U$, using conjugation through $\lambda$ for its $\mathbf G_m$-actions and the fixed points $e_X,1$. The source has the geometry established in step 4. The target is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type by the definition of $R_u(B)$, and the differential is the isomorphism of step 4. All source tangent weights are strictly positive. Hence $m$ is an isomorphism of $F$-schemes, with the $T$-equivariance already proved. The argument never changes the chosen order. If $r=0$, the source is $\operatorname{Spec}F$, step 3 gives $\operatorname{Lie}(U)=0$, and the same inverse lemma applies with the empty set of weights. Its isomorphism is the unit section, so $U=1$.

source.place: 21.68(a), last sentences of proof, p.445, referring to Corollary 13.42, p.270; Remark 21.69, p.446, permits any order.
